extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions' Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, campus legal counsel, and higher-education administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for designing and implementing postsecondary institutions' grievance procedures for sex-based harassment under Title IX, covering disclosures, privacy, live-questioning/hearing formats, FERPA interaction, impartiality, and procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on disclosures of information obtained solely through grievance procedures (§106.46(e)(6)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(e)(6)(iii) is narrowly framed to address privacy concerns related to information and evidence obtained solely through the grievance procedures; disclosures of such information are limited unless authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may authorize narrow disclosures to particular individuals or of particular pieces of evidence depending on circumstances; must ensure parties and advisors are aware of permissible and prohibited disclosures; must satisfy §106.45(b)(5) obligation to take reasonable steps to protect privacy. Reasonable steps may include policies that protect sensitive evidence and software that restricts further distribution. Widespread disclosures of information obtained solely through grievance procedures would likely violate §106.45(b)(5). The Department added a sentence clarifying that disclosures for administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint are authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections must not restrict participation (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(5) prohibits recipients from taking steps to protect privacy that restrict the parties' ability to gather evidence, consult with family/confidential resources/advisors, or otherwise prepare for or participate in the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While institutions must protect privacy, such protections cannot impede a party's ability to participate; authorized disclosures under §106.46(e)(6)(iii) include those permitted under §106.45(b)(5). Institutions should balance privacy protections with ensuring meaningful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions must take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are required to address unauthorized disclosures of information obtained solely through the sex-based harassment grievance procedures; this may include penalizing unauthorized disclosures but the Department declines to mandate penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps to prevent/address unauthorized disclosures may include restrictions on use and redisclosure, limits on physical copies, policies, and software controls. Institutions should consider circumstances when responding to unauthorized disclosures and may use discipline but are not required by regulation to impose penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized disclosures for administrative proceedings or litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of information and evidence obtained through the grievance procedures for purposes of administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint of sex-based harassment are authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule explicitly permits such disclosures and the preamble clarifies the Department does not intend to limit parties' exercise of legal rights (e.g., filing an OCR complaint or initiating/defending litigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA interaction and GEPA/constitutional overrides
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent Title IX regulations require disclosure of information from education records that would not comply with FERPA, the GEPA override (and constitutional override in some circumstances) applies and requires disclosure under §106.46(e)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department maintains that parties and their advisors must have equal opportunity to access evidence. Where evidence consists of education records not directly related to a student (and thus the student could not consent), a GEPA override permits sharing with parties' advisors similarly to the constitutional override. Institutions should follow the GEPA/constitutional override framework when FERPA would otherwise prevent disclosure required by Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access evidence (parties and advisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must provide the parties and their advisors with an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible, rather than providing access only to the parties and allowing them to choose whether to share with advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing advisors access is efficient given parties choose advisors to assist in the procedures. Institutions may provide either access to the relevant evidence or the same written investigative report that accurately summarizes the evidence and must provide access to the evidence upon request if they provide a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on redisclosure and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.46(e)(6)(iii) institutions must take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures, which may include restrictions on parties' and advisors' use of information and evidence and limitations on their ability to receive physical copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERPA does not limit an eligible student's use or redisclosure of their own education records, but Title IX permits institutions to limit redistribution of evidence obtained solely through grievance procedures. Examples include software that restricts distribution and institutional policies restricting further sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live-questioning process requirement (§106.46(f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: All postsecondary institutions must be required to provide a live-questioning process that enables the decisionmaker to assess the credibility of parties and witnesses if credibility is in dispute and relevant to evaluating one or more allegations of sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The live-questioning process must be provided either through (1) individual meetings with the investigator or decisionmaker, who will ask initial and follow-up questions proposed by the parties and the investigator's/decisionmaker's own questions, or (2) a live hearing with questions, including party-proposed questions, asked by the decisionmaker or the party's advisor. This approach balances equity, meaningful opportunity to be heard, and institutional diversity in size/resources. Regardless of format, each party must have the opportunity to have relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions asked and the investigator/decisionmaker must consider all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest and bias (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX prohibits any Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker from having a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.8(d)(2) requires training on serving impartially, including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias. These safeguards apply irrespective of the live-questioning format chosen by an institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and impartiality requirements (§106.8(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: All investigators, decisionmakers, and other individuals responsible for implementing grievance procedures must be trained on how to serve impartially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must include avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias. Proper training supports reliable outcomes and confidence in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of parties and presumption of non-responsibility (§106.45(b)(1) & (b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat parties equitably and require a presumption that the respondent is not responsible until a determination is made at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are foundational procedural protections and work alongside live-questioning and evidence-access provisions to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must perform an objective evaluation of all evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties to the requirement to provide equal access to relevant evidence or an investigative report summarizing it, and to consider party-proposed questions and follow-ups during live questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for institutions in selecting live-questioning format
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may choose whether to use live hearings with questioning by an advisor or some other form of live questioning based on their administrative structure, resources, and applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department permits flexibility to balance burdens and benefits; institutions must still comply with Title IX and the final regulations. States and institutions can provide additional procedures so long as they do not conflict with Title IX. When deciding, institutions may consider costs (staffing, training, advisors, potential litigation) and benefits (credibility assessment, fairness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of impact on reporting and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department recognizes that requirements like advisor-conducted cross-examination may chill reporting of sex-based harassment and affect parties' willingness to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In setting procedures, institutions should weigh chilling effects and trauma concerns against accuracy and procedural protections; permitting but not requiring advisor-conducted hearings is intended to mitigate chilling while preserving options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathews-type due process balancing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of required procedures considered Mathews factors: the private interest of the affected individual, the risk of erroneous deprivation and benefit of additional procedures, and the government's interest including burden and cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considered these factors (including lasting impact on respondents, risk of error, participation incentives, and institutional burdens) in deciding to require live questioning but allow flexibility in format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of Title IX procedures relative to court-like trials
rubrics_metrics.description: School disciplinary proceedings are not civil or criminal trials and therefore do not need to provide the same panoply of procedural protections as courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some procedural protections are required (notice, meaningful opportunity to be heard, impartiality), institutions may tailor procedures appropriate to administrative disciplinary context rather than replicate courtroom procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for parties to seek support and consult confidants
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(b)(5) prohibits recipients from taking steps to protect privacy that restrict a party's ability to consult with family members or seek support from friends; disclosures to family members are authorized under §106.46(e)(6)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, §106.46(e)(6)(iii) prohibits a party from disclosing information obtained solely through the grievance procedures to friends unless the institution expressly authorizes such disclosure, complies with privacy obligations, and the disclosure does not violate other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists not restricted by §106.46(e)(6)(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(e)(6)(iii) requires institutions to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures by parties and their advisors but does not impose any restrictions on journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision is limited to information obtained solely through the grievance procedures and obligations apply to parties and advisors, not to press reporting based on other means.
